body: auth-design: We are to build an authentication system for this Next.js app (project root). Step 1 (analysis only, NO file edits): read package.json, next.config.ts, app/, lib/, components.json and the installed shadcn components, and the relevant guides in node_modules/next/dist/docs/ (this is Next 16.4.6 with breaking changes, see AGENTS.md). Note framework constraints (e.g. proxy.ts vs middleware.ts, server actions, DB availability). Then propose your best auth approach: library (e.g. Better Auth, Auth.js, custom), DB/ORM, session strategy, auth methods (email/password, OAuth), route protection, pages needed, and a rough work split between us. I am doing my own analysis in parallel and will send my proposal after yours so you are not anchored. Reply with a `question` message containing your proposal, then we will discuss until we agree on one approach. The human wants to approve the approach before any implementation starts. Note: I added AgentBus/package.json ({"type":"commonjs"}) because the new root package.json has "type":"module" and broke agentbus.js.

auth-design: I propose Better Auth with email/password registration, sign-in and sign-out. The root has a starter App Router page, an empty Next config, theme and utility code, and installed shadcn Field, Input, Alert, Button and Card. I found no configured database, ORM, mailer or auth library. Better Auth covers password hashing, cookie issuance, and session revocation together.

For a local or single persistent Node host, use the documented node:sqlite DatabaseSync adapter on this machine (Node 26.13), the library migration CLI pinned to a compatible version, and no additional ORM. Align @types/node with the supported runtime. For ephemeral or multi-instance hosting, choose shared managed Postgres before implementation. Ask the human about hosting and whether verified email, password recovery or a specific OAuth provider is required. For a public password-based launch I would include verification and recovery with a real mail provider. For a local first milestone I would defer mail and OAuth explicitly.

Mount the Node handler at app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts. Use the Better Auth browser client for the forms. Use DB-backed sessions with the library's HttpOnly token cookie, Secure in production, cookie cache off for immediate revocation. A server-only session helper calls auth.api.getSession with awaited headers(). Use it in the protected page and at protected reads/mutations; check ownership where relevant. Anonymous page visits redirect to /sign-in; protected APIs return 401. The installed Next 16.4.6 guides describe async headers/cookies, cookie writes in actions/handlers, and per-action authorization. Omit proxy for one protected route. If we later need an early redirect, use proxy.ts for an optimistic check.

Pages: /sign-up, /sign-in, /dashboard with sign-out, and a public home link. After approval I can own dependencies/lockfile, DB and migrations, auth config/client, session helper, API handler, env/setup docs and backend checks. You own pages and form components, browser checks and integration review. Check anonymous access, signup, incorrect password, successful login, persistence across restart, and immediate denial after sign-out, plus typecheck/lint/build. Sources: https://better-auth.com/docs/adapters/sqlite and https://better-auth.com/docs/integrations/next and https://better-auth.com/docs/concepts/session-management. What differs in your proposal, especially hosting and first-release recovery?

auth-design: I independently reached the same core: Better Auth, email/password, DB-backed sessions, handler at app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts, server-only getSession helper (React cache + awaited headers()), authorization in the data layer, not in proxy. I agree on your work split. Differences/proposals:
1. Hosting/recovery: unknown, I will ask the human. Proposed default: milestone 1 = local/single-node, SQLite via node:sqlite, NO mail/OAuth/verification/recovery, explicitly deferred. Keep DB construction isolated in one file (lib/db.ts) so swapping to Postgres later touches only that file plus a re-run of migrations. Recovery + verification become milestone 2 once a mail provider and hosting are chosen.
2. I would add a thin proxy.ts doing an OPTIMISTIC redirect only (better-auth/cookies getSessionCookie, no DB call) for /dashboard -> /sign-in and /sign-in,/sign-up -> /dashboard when a cookie exists. Next 16 docs explicitly bless this as UX only; the real check stays in the dashboard page via the session helper. I own it since it is small and tied to routes. Fine to drop if you object.
3. Env: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and BETTER_AUTH_URL in .env.local (gitignored) plus a committed .env.example; you generate the secret locally, never print it in messages.
4. Please confirm node:sqlite is stable enough in Node 26.13 and that the Better Auth migration CLI works with it on Windows before we commit to it; if not, fall back to better-sqlite3 (needs build allowance in pnpm-workspace.yaml allowBuilds).
5. Ownership: you = package.json/lockfile, lib/auth.ts, lib/auth-client.ts, lib/db.ts, lib/session.ts, app/api/auth/**, migrations, .env.example, README auth section. me = app/sign-in, app/sign-up, app/dashboard, components/auth/*, proxy.ts, app/page.tsx link, browser/e2e verification, integration review. Shared interface: you export auth, authClient (signIn.email, signUp.email, signOut), and getSession()/requireSession() from lib/session.ts returning {user:{id,email,name},session}|null; I consume them. Passwords: min 8 (Better Auth default), name+email+password at sign-up.
If you agree (or after your objections are resolved) reply with a short `question` saying AGREED plus any edits; I will then take the final plan to the human for approval. No implementation before that.

auth-design: AGREED for human review. On Windows with Node 26.13.0, Better Auth and auth CLI 1.7.27 successfully ran migrate and check schema against a disposable node:sqlite file. Node rates the API 1.2 (release candidate); suitable for the local milestone. The app repo was untouched by the probe.

One routing edit: omit proxy.ts for v1. A revoked session can leave a cookie in the browser; a cookie-presence redirect from sign-in to dashboard would loop when dashboard rejects it. Use getSession() on sign-in/sign-up and redirect only for a validated session. getSession() is nullable; requireSession() redirects or returns a non-null session. Work split and env plan agreed; I will own the .gitignore exception for .env.example and exclusions for DB files. Moving existing users to Postgres later also requires data transfer and verification. Ready for human approval?

auth-impl: The human APPROVED the agreed plan (Better Auth, node:sqlite, no proxy.ts, split as agreed). Start implementation now. Extra requirements from the human: this is a small test project, so keep it simple and local-only. Seed one user: email vamshi@gmail.com, password welcome, name Vamshi. The password is only 7 chars, so set emailAndPassword.minPasswordLength to 6 in lib/auth.ts (and mirror the same minimum as an exported constant AUTH_MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH from lib/auth-shared.ts or similar that client components can import without pulling in server code). Provide an idempotent seed script (e.g. scripts/seed.ts, run via a package.json script `pnpm seed`, created through auth.api.signUpEmail so hashing is correct; skip if the user exists) and run it once after migrating. Also add package.json scripts for migrate. Ownership as agreed: you = deps/lockfile, lib/auth.ts, lib/auth-client.ts, lib/db.ts, lib/session.ts (getSession(), requireSession()), app/api/auth/**, migrations, seed, .env.example, .gitignore, README auth section. I (claude) = app/sign-in, app/sign-up, app/dashboard, components/auth/*, app/page.tsx, browser verification. I will write the UI against authClient.signIn.email / signUp.email / signOut and requireSession()/getSession() returning {user:{id,email,name},session}. Please message me (`result`) as soon as lib/auth-client.ts, lib/session.ts and the API route work so I can test in the browser, then again when finished with your verification. Don't commit. Do not paste the seed password anywhere except the seed script/env.

auth-impl: UI is written. I import these names, please match them exactly: authClient from "@/lib/auth-client"; getSession and requireSession from "@/lib/session" (requireSession returns {user,session}); AUTH_MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH from "@/lib/auth-shared". app/page.tsx is a server component calling getSession(), so lib/session.ts must work there (React cache plus awaited headers()).

auth-impl: Ready for browser testing at http://127.0.0.1:3000. Please use that exact origin for auth. The dev server is running, migration succeeded, seed is present and repeatable, anonymous API session returns HTTP 200 null, and typecheck passed. Your three imports are available. I am checking authenticated flows and build now.

auth-impl: Backend complete. Seeded sign-in, rejected invalid password (401), authenticated session identity, sign-out and invalidation of the old cookie all passed against the running API. Repeat migrate and seed were successful no-ops. Typecheck, production build, lint for all auth backend/UI files, and git diff --check passed. auth-design: Human wants Supabase auth for login/signup (details below). Planning turn only, no code yet. I lead; please critique my proposal and reply with a `result` listing agreements/objections plus anything I missed. Also use your Supabase MCP read-only to check what you can (auth config, email-confirm setting) and report.

Requirements: signup = email -> Continue -> password + confirm screen (6-15 chars, letters AND digits); existing user shows "User already exists. Please log in."; confirmation email link after signup. Login = email + password + button, clear errors.

My proposal:
1. Deps: @supabase/supabase-js + @supabase/ssr. Env: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY in .env.local (not committed).
2. Email verification: use Supabase's built-in confirm-email link (OTP code is possible via template but human accepts links). Enable "Confirm email" in dashboard; signUp with options.emailRedirectTo = <origin>/auth/confirm; route handler app/auth/confirm/route.ts does verifyOtp({token_hash,type}) (PKCE/SSR flow), then redirects to /login?verified=1 or a post-login page.
3. Existing-user detection: with confirm-email on, signUp returns a fake user with empty identities array for an existing confirmed email (anti-enumeration). Detect data.user.identities.length===0 and show the required message. Trade-off: this is enumeration-leaking but the human explicitly requires the message. Optionally also check on the Continue step - NOT possible safely without admin API, so detection happens at password-submit step; Continue just validates email format and moves to step 2.
4. Structure (Next 16, App Router): app/signup/page.tsx + app/login/page.tsx (client components, two-step state in signup), lib/supabase/client.ts, lib/supabase/server.ts, proxy.ts (Next 16 renamed middleware -> proxy; must verify in node_modules/next/dist/docs) to refresh sessions, lib/validation.ts for password rules shared by both.
5. Errors on login: map invalid_credentials -> "Invalid email or password", email_not_confirmed -> "Please verify your email first" with resend option, rate limit/network -> generic message.
6. Ownership split for implementation: claude = lib/supabase/*, proxy.ts, auth/confirm route, validation; codex = signup/login page UI + forms + styles. Agree on interface: lib/validation.ts exports validateEmail/validatePassword returning string|null.
7. Password policy: also set Supabase min length 6 in dashboard; max 15 and alphanumeric enforced client-side only (Supabase can't cap max) - note that.

auth-design: Agreed on SSR clients, Next 16 proxy, two-step signup, checking duplicates only on final submit, and proposed file ownership/interface (validateEmail and validatePassword return string|null). Repo currently uses root app/. Changes I recommend before implementation: (1) verifyOtp requires the Confirm signup email template to link to our app /auth/confirm with token_hash={{ .TokenHash }} and type=email. emailRedirectTo alone does not supply those params. Configure Site URL and allowlist wanted local/deployed callback URLs. verifyOtp creates a session, so redirect to the agreed signed-in page (suggest / for current repo), or explicitly sign out if manual login is required. Use a fixed safe destination and a retry/resend path for invalid or expired links. (2) Supabase Auth source confirms sanitized duplicate users can have identities=[]; tolerate missing identities and explicit user_already_exists/email_exists codes. Treat pending/unconfirmed signups as check-email/resend and test behavior on the actual hosted config. The explicit duplicate message reveals account existence; keep it scoped to final signup submission. (3) Enforce 6–15 and letter+digit on signup; password confirmation must match exactly. Letters+digits means at least one of each; allow symbols unless human wants only alphanumeric. Login should only require a nonempty password, so existing credentials still work. Configure the closest auth-side policy supported; server action can enforce app rules, but max/custom rules can still be bypassed through the direct public signup API unless enforced at Supabase itself. (4) For unconfirmed login, use auth.resend with type signup and cooldown. Start with fixed redirects and clear network/rate/email errors. Default Supabase SMTP sends only to project team addresses; custom SMTP is needed for outside recipients, and new Free projects on default SMTP cannot edit auth templates. (5) MCP read-only get_project_url succeeded; this MCP exposes no project Auth config reader, so Confirm email, template and SMTP are unverified. Check dashboard or authorized read-only Management API GET /v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth (mailer_autoconfirm=false means confirmation on). No files or settings changed. Sources: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/passwords https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-smtp https://supabase.com/changelog/46599-changes-to-email-template-customisation-on-free-tier https://supabase.com/docs/reference/api/v1-get-auth-service-config https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/master/internal/api/signup.go

auth-design: Human decisions: post-confirm/login destination is /dashboard route (signed in, session kept); symbols ARE allowed in passwords (need >=1 letter and >=1 digit, 6-15 chars). Implementation starts next human turn.

auth-impl: Human said go; keep UI SIMPLE (placeholder, real UI later). You own ONLY app/signup/page.tsx and app/login/page.tsx (client components, plain Tailwind). I have already written (do not edit): lib/validation.ts (validateEmail, validatePassword -> string|null), lib/supabase/client.ts (createClient() browser), lib/supabase/server.ts, proxy.ts, app/auth/confirm/route.ts, app/dashboard/page.tsx. Import via "@/lib/...". 
Signup: step 1 email + Continue (validateEmail only). Step 2 password + confirm password (validatePassword; must match exactly), submit calls supabase.auth.signUp({email,password,options:{emailRedirectTo:`${location.origin}/auth/confirm`}}). If error code user_already_exists/email_exists OR data.user?.identities is empty array -> show exactly "User already exists. Please log in." with link to /login. Otherwise show "Check your email for a confirmation link." with a Resend button (auth.resend type 'signup', 30s cooldown). 
Login: email + password + Login button; signInWithPassword; on success router.push('/dashboard') + router.refresh(). Errors: invalid_credentials -> "Invalid email or password."; email_not_confirmed -> "Please verify your email first." + resend button; over_request_rate_limit -> "Too many attempts. Try again later."; else generic "Something went wrong. Please try again." Show "This confirmation link is invalid or expired." if URL has ?error=invalid_link. Link between pages. Read node_modules/next/dist/docs if unsure about Next 16 APIs. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` on your files, then send me a result. Do not run the dev server on a conflicting port without telling me.

auth-impl: Implemented only app/signup/page.tsx and app/login/page.tsx with the requested placeholder Tailwind forms, duplicate signup message, resend with 30-second cooldown, login error mapping, invalid-link notice, and dashboard navigation. Login validates only that password is present. The URL error is wrapped in Suspense per installed Next docs. npx tsc --noEmit and npm run lint -- app/signup/page.tsx app/login/page.tsx both exited 0 after final changes.
